title: Mahesh Kumar Singh v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Vikram Nath, J.; Krishna Pratap Singh, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; petitioner relegated to Clause 6.5 objections.
headnote: A writ petition disputing an electricity demand bill is not entertained where the consumer has a statutory remedy of filing objections under Clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The petition was dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.
facts: Mahesh Kumar Singh filed a writ petition in the Allahabad High Court challenging a demand raised by bill dated 25 March 2017. Counsel for the State and for the distribution-licensee respondents (respondent Nos. 2 and 3) submitted that the petitioner had a statutory remedy of filing objections under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005. After hearing both sides, the Division Bench declined to entertain the petition.

holding_units.holding: A writ petition disputing a demand bill is not entertained when the consumer has a statutory remedy of filing objections under Clause 6.5 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005; the petition is dismissed with liberty to avail that remedy.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the demand raised by bill dated 25.03.2017
not_decided.note: Merits of the bill were not examined; petitioner was left to Clause 6.5 objections.
